questions.q: How do NAV commands differ from DO commands?
options: DO commands work only on planes and in Rover
NAV is where to fly, DO is what to do
They do not differ, they are synonyms
NAV commands are used only for takeoff
questions.explain: NAV commands set where to fly; DO commands set what to do along the way without changing the route. A mission moves from NAV to NAV.

questions.q: Which altitude frame does an ordinary mission need?
options: Absolute, above sea level
Relative to home
Always above terrain
Any will do
questions.explain: An absolute altitude easily gives an error of hundreds of meters.

options: Where the pilot stands
Where the vehicle armed
Where the ground station is
The first waypoint of the mission
questions.explain: After you move, home stays in the old place, so reset it before takeoff.

questions.q: What is the code of MAV_CMD_NAV_WAYPOINT?
questions.explain: 16 is WAYPOINT, 22 is TAKEOFF, 20 is RTL, 21 is LAND.

It moves the home location

questions.q: Which altitude frame is safe when you change sites?
options: Altitude in feet
Above home or above terrain
Any, it makes no difference
Absolute, above sea level from GPS
questions.explain: Absolute altitudes are the classic crash.

questions.q: A copter mission is uploaded, but in Auto from the ground the vehicle does not take off as expected. What is wrong with the first items?
questions.fragment:
seq cmd                  frame          alt
0   HOME                 GLOBAL         0
1   NAV_WAYPOINT         RELATIVE_ALT   20
2   NAV_WAYPOINT         RELATIVE_ALT   20
3   NAV_RETURN_TO_LAUNCH
options: There is no NAV_TAKEOFF: a copter mission that starts on the ground must begin with a takeoff command
Items 1 and 2 have the same altitude, and in Auto a copter requires an altitude change between adjacent mission waypoints
RELATIVE_ALT cannot be mixed with a HOME in GLOBAL: every item needs the same frame
NAV_RETURN_TO_LAUNCH is not allowed at the end: a mission must end with NAV_LAND
questions.explain: When starting from the ground the first navigation item is TAKEOFF; that makes the behavior unambiguous.
